sections.name: A little / I understand a little

events.text: Welcome to Lesson One. In a moment you'll hear a short conversation between two women in Bangkok. One of them has just moved to the city. Don't worry about understanding it yet — just listen to the sound of it.

ได้นิดหน่อยค่ะ

เข้าใจนิดหน่อยค่ะ พูดช้าๆ หน่อยได้มั้ยคะ
ได้ค่ะ
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to hold that conversation yourself. Let's start with the very first thing you heard.
Here's how a woman gets someone's attention politely — excuse me.
ขอโทษค่ะ
Listen again, and notice the ending.
ขอโทษค่ะ
That last sound — kâ — is a small polite word that women add to the end of what they say. You'll use it constantly. Say it with me. Just the ending.
ค่ะ
ค่ะ
Now the first part. It has two pieces. Say the second piece first.

Now the first piece.

Again.

ภาษา
ภาษา

Now — do you understand? To turn it into a question, you add a short rising question word, and then the polite ending. Listen to the whole question.
เข้าใจมั้ยคะ
Notice the ending changed. In a question, it's ká — with a rising sound. Say the ending of the question.
มั้ยคะ
มั้ยคะ
Now ask — do you understand?

เข้าใจมั้ยคะ

His ending was khráp. That's the male polite word — the same job as your kâ. You'll hear it all the time. You don't say it; you say kâ. Answer him — you don't understand.
